doc.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013

title: Milt Hinton and the New York Bass Choir
summary: Reid describes Hinton's positive aura and their first meeting at Bill Lee's house with the Bass Choir.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I’ve been very fortunate to get to know a few of those people, like Milt Hinton. Do you have words to describe what it was like to be around him and that generation of players?

Wow. It was very fulfilling to be around him, in every way. I mean he seemed to satisfy everything you were wondering about, it was not a mystery, it was just there. He had an aura about him that was so positive, and everything was positive. I never saw him — I was around him a lot. We used to go visit him in his home when he was declining. But he still was amazing. But when he was on, you know, earlier in years he was playing, it was a true, it was just honest stuff. He wasn’t trying to show off, he just did what he did. But you were saying whoa. Then you said, “Do you know how old he is?” Yeah, and he played better — but he loved to play the bass. If you played bass, even if you just bought your bass that day, you were part of the family. And he was that kind of person. But when I first met him, it was like I’d known him for years. It was with the New York Bass Choir in New York and I got a chance to go to Bill Lee’s house over in Brooklyn at ten o’clock in the morning on a Saturday, and Milt was there, and it was incredible. Richard Davis and Bill Lee and Lyle Atkinson. Ron Carter didn’t come that day but it was incredible. And then they finished. And I didn’t know where I was. I knew I was in Brooklyn but I didn’t know where I was. And I was staying in Manhattan in a hotel. So I said, “Can anybody show me how to get to the subway?” I found my way there and Milt © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

said, “Well I’m going now, come on with me.” And we walked, and I had to walk faster to keep up with him. And that’s how our relationship, from that day, it was perfect. He was really, really, really wonderful.
